problem_statement: The Surjith S M documentation HTML template, already rebranded as 'Tidewheel Deploy CLI Documentation' (a static single-page developer guide for a command-line deploy tool), is a directly runnable static site (index.html, css/*, js/*, local images, no build step) with a fixed dark-mode toggle, a hero, a left docs sidebar navigation that scrolls to eleven guide sections (Getting Started, Installing the CLI, Authenticating Your Account, Recommended Adapters, Configuring a Project, Preview Deploys, Using the Config File, Support Desk, Files & Sources, Version History, and Copyright and license), and a wide content column. Add the docs site's own section-navigation feature: (1) a 'Guide finder' scope filter at the top of the docs sidebar with topic chips (All / Setup / Configure / Reference) and a live '.gfinder__readout' 'Showing N of 11 topics' readout, wired end to end so clicking a scope chip filters which sidebar section links are shown AND updates the readout to reflect the selection (e.g. clicking Configure filters the sidebar to the three Configure-phase sections and sets the readout to 'Showing 3 of 11 topics . Configure'); and (2) a shared 'Guide finder rail' component that appears consistently in THREE regions of the page - inside the docs sidebar (.gfinder-rail--sidebar), in the introduction (.gfinder-rail--intro), and in the Copyright-and-license section (.gfinder-rail--license) - so a reader anywhere in the guide can jump to a phase. The filter panel and the rail must keep the template's clean light docs palette (teal #16a085 accent, ink text on paper) and be responsive so the page has NO horizontal overflow on the 390px mobile viewport. Preserve the Tidewheel hero, the docs sidebar navigation, all eleven guide sections with their code samples and thumbnail images, the dark-mode toggle, the prettyPhoto lightbox assets, and the footer license.
required_content: Keep the rebranded Tidewheel Deploy CLI hero, the left docs sidebar navigation, and all eleven guide sections (Getting Started through Copyright and license) with their code samples and local thumbnail images.

Add a 'Guide finder' scope filter at the top of the docs sidebar: an eyebrow 'Guide finder', the heading 'Scope the guide', four scope chips (All / Setup / Configure / Reference) inside a '.gfinder__chips' container, and a live '.gfinder__readout' 'Showing N of 11 topics' readout.

Add a shared 'Guide finder rail' component (eyebrow 'GUIDE FINDER' + phase links Setup / Configure / Reference) consistently in THREE regions - inside the docs sidebar (.gfinder-rail--sidebar), in the introduction (.gfinder-rail--intro), and in the Copyright-and-license section (.gfinder-rail--license) - so the same component appears in each region, not only in one.

Style the Guide finder panel and the shared rail to match the template's clean light docs look (teal #16a085 accent, ink text on a light panel) - the rendered filter panel and sidebar must be visually faithful to the reference, not a collapsed, overlapping, or dark-on-dark restyle.

Make the Guide finder responsive so the page has NO horizontal overflow on the 390px mobile viewport (let the scope chips wrap / use a fluid layout instead of a fixed-width non-wrapping row); do not merely clip the overflow with overflow-x:hidden - the document itself must not exceed the mobile viewport width. Keep desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) free of overflow.

Keep the Guide finder fully wired end to end: clicking a scope chip (Configure / Setup / All) must update the '.gfinder__readout' to reflect the selection (e.g. clicking Configure yields 'Showing 3 of 11 topics . Configure'), in addition to highlighting the active chip and hiding the non-matching sidebar section links - the post-click terminal state must reflect the selected scope, not the default 'Showing 11 of 11 topics . All'.

Do not damage the existing Tidewheel hero, the docs sidebar navigation, the eleven guide sections, the code samples, the local thumbnail images, the dark-mode toggle, or the footer license; keep the branding.
design_constraints: Keep the template's clean light docs visual language (teal #16a085 accent, ink text on paper, the sidebar / content-column rhythm); the Guide finder panel and rail must look native to the docs sidebar, not a bolted-on benchmark strip.
Do not replace the documentation page, the docs sidebar, or the guide sections with a new app shell, framework, external design system, or unrelated layout.
Do not remove the Guide finder panel, the four scope chips, the shared rail, the sidebar navigation, the guide sections, the hero, or the filter script.

Do not add npm dependencies, remote scripts, remote fonts, remote images, generated build outputs, or unrelated file churn; keep the static architecture (index.html, css/guidefinder.css, and the js/guidefinder.js interaction script).
The Guide finder panel and rail must fit within 1440px desktop, 834px tablet, and 390px mobile viewports without horizontal overflow, and render in the light teal/ink docs palette.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial capture the rebranded Tidewheel hero and the docs page above the fold.

desktop_guide_finder and mobile_guide_finder scroll to the Guide finder panel + docs sidebar and verify the 'Scope the guide' heading, the scope chips, and the readout render in the light teal palette on desktop and 390px mobile (the visual-fidelity states).

desktop_configure_scope / desktop_setup_scope / desktop_all_reset / mobile_configure_scope click the scope chips and verify the '.gfinder__readout' updates to reflect the selection (the interaction-trajectory states); their before-state is desktop_guide_finder.

desktop_intro_region scrolls to the introduction and desktop_license_region scrolls to the Copyright-and-license section; both verify the shared 'Guide finder rail' (.gfinder-rail--intro / .gfinder-rail--license) is present, proving the component appears consistently across regions (desktop_sidebar_region covers the sidebar placement).
desktop_getting_started, desktop_plugins, desktop_support and desktop_changelog check the guide sections, code samples, and local thumbnail imagery survive.

Baseline captures still complete (the page structure is intact); a fixed-width non-wrapping chip row, a rail present only in the sidebar, a collapsed dark-on-dark overlapping panel, or a filter that does not re-sync its readout are scored as overflow / cross-section / visual / interaction failures, not capture failures.

change_completion: The Guide finder scope filter (four scope chips + readout) sits at the top of the docs sidebar.
The shared 'Guide finder rail' appears in the sidebar, introduction, and license regions.
On mobile the page has no horizontal overflow after the responsive layout.
content_asset_continuity: The guide stays grounded in the repo's local thumbnail / plugin images (images/upload/*.png); no external or placeholder media.
The Tidewheel hero, docs sidebar, guide sections, code samples, and footer license are preserved.
design_consistency: The Guide finder panel and shared rail keep the light teal/ink docs style and are visually faithful to the reference.
The same Guide finder rail is consistent across the sidebar / introduction / license regions; the hero, sidebar, and sections remain recognizable.
interaction_continuity: Clicking a scope chip updates the 'Showing N of 11 topics' readout to the selection (the post-click terminal state reflects the change, not the default).
The All-scope reset restores the full eleven-section view and readout.
regression: The Tidewheel hero, docs sidebar, guide sections, code samples, thumbnails, dark-mode toggle, and footer license retain their branding and imagery.
No package, build system, backend, remote asset, generated build artifact, or broad redesign is introduced. Hidden text, fake asset references, or a simplified mock must not pass.
responsive: The page has no horizontal overflow on the 390px mobile states.
Desktop and tablet states remain free of horizontal overflow.

author_notes: Repo-grounded static Bootstrap documentation template. capability=Repair mobile horizontal-overflow. The only file that differs between the broken (baseline) and repaired (reference) page is css/quickstart.css, which styles a new Quickstart checklist strip mounted at the top of the Getting Started section in index.html. Content and DOM are byte-identical across reference/baseline/bad; the sole discriminator is no_horizontal_overflow (tolerance 24) on mobile_gs (reference 0px, baseline 345px, bad 165px). The strip markup and the css/quickstart.css link are declared infrastructure, identical across all three legs. Served directly as static files; reference is runtime-clean (0 console, 0 network, 0 overflow) across all six captured home/getting-started states.

metadata.defect: Quickstart checklist strip fixed-width nowrap tile row causes mobile horizontal overflow on the documentation page
